strategy_notes: CONCENTRATED MOMENTUM PHASE — Portfolio shifting to sector-concentrated approach in semiconductors + AI beneficiaries. Key rules: (1) When a sector shows 3+ names surging >5% simultaneously, it's a confirmed sector breakout — concentrate positions there rather than diversifying across weak sectors. (2) Cut non-confirmers by day 3-4 without hesitation — ORCL and ADBE losses were predictable from relative weakness signals. (3) Scale winners: AMD's +19% gain justifies holding past normal +7% threshold when sector momentum is accelerating (multiple names confirming). (4) Profit-taking levels: take 50% at +15%, hold remainder with trailing stop at +10%. (5) For new entries in hot sectors, size at 15-20% not 10% when 3+ sector names confirm. (6) Maintain max 2 sectors for concentration with at least 1 diversifier. (7) Immediate sell triggers: -4% from entry OR relative weakness (underperforming QQQ by >2%) on a strong market day.

last_decision.self_reflection: AMD is the star position at +18.95%, validating my pilot entry thesis and my lesson that semiconductor sector momentum is durable when multiple names confirm. ORCL (-8.84%) and ADBE (-6.14%) are concerning — enterprise software is underperforming badly relative to semis. AAPL (-0.60%) is flat/weak. AVGO (+1.65%) is modest. The key lesson: sector selection matters enormously. I deployed equally across semis and enterprise software, but semis massively outperformed. I should have concentrated more in the strongest sector. ORCL's -3.24% today while AMD gained +14.85% is a clear relative weakness signal — I should have cut ORCL earlier per my 'cut non-confirmers by day 4' rule. With 2 days elapsed since entry, ORCL and ADBE are already showing the pattern of immediate post-entry reversal that I identified as an early exit signal in Lesson Batch 1.
